events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Axes High

tip: As leader: +5% Unit Trait Modifier / Infantry
As general: +10% Unit Trait Modifier / Infantry

options.text: Be bold and aggressive.
Stay vigilant and on the defence.

events.text: As forges fill the royal armory with new steel weapons, your heir, [character], seems eager to take up an an axe against our foes. What shall we tell him?

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Budding Archer

options.text: Sharpen your vision.

tip: As leader: +10% Height From Modifier / Hill
As general: +25% Height From Modifier / Hill

options.text: Use the terrain to your advantage.

events.text: [character] has developed an interest in the new technological advances in archery, and he comes to you for advice. What do you tell the budding sharpshooter?

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Early Adopters

options.text: Increase output from mines and quarries.
Improve training practices for ranged infantry.
Study the latest advances in combat.

events.text: The completion of the first windlass has proven to be a boon to inventors, who imagine a wide variety of uses for the apparatus. Many of these clever individuals have flocked to court to convince of us their ideas, but we should consider each request carefully.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Maiden Voyage

options.text: Build supply boats for laborers and traders.
Build pleasure yachts for the noble families.
Build crude warships and train in combat.

events.text: With the development of the Lateen Sail, the court is eager to expand its reach over the mysterious seas. Yet there is disagreement over what types of vessels should be built for our maiden voyages. What we choose will show the world how we plan to utilize this powerful new technology.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Monism

options.text: Then there is only one conclusion - if movement is impossible, distance and separation and change are but illusions, and all the universe is in fact one unity.
But... we do move. This cannot be right, I must think harder on the problem.
Fortunately, I don't fancy a trip to [city].

events.text: Suppose that you wish to walk to [city]. Before you can reach the half way point of the journey, you must first reach the one-quarter journey point. And before you reach that, you must first finish one-eighth of the journey. And so on, for each new, smaller distance you imagine. Thus, you cannot begin to walk at all.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Piracy Powers

options.text: Institute the security measures.
Give the barbarians their space.

events.text: After careful examination, [character] has devised an ingenious method of reducing piracy along [rival] trade routes. However, some of the local tribes rely on casual banditry for survival. Shall we go forward with this new policy, or do we leave well enough alone?

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Seeking Adumbration

leadsTo.name: The Gods do not Play Dice

options.text: That's a fantastic idea!
That's a terrible idea!

events.text: "So... you ever gambled with a priestess?" [character] asks over his third wine cup. "I mean, they are supposed to see the omens and future and all that, yeah? So how come they're never rolling the bones?" He pauses for a long contemplative look in his drink. "But we don't have to wonder! You're the gods-damned [title]! We go find one right now, bring out the dice, see what they got, eh?"

events.author: Soren Johnson
events.name: Slavery Now?

options.text: Enact Slavery as an institution.
There will be no slaves in [rival].

events.text: The court has opened debate on the topic of labor, and are of two minds on the matter. We can adopt the practice of Slavery, or we can keep Freedom in [rival]. What shall we decree?

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Soul and Body

options.text: And so we may be parted with our bodies, but not our divine souls. A beautiful thought.
And suppose a soul did require a physical body? We could, in that case, just as easily not sense the body, but still require it for our thoughts and soul.

events.text: As debate and writing blossom throughout [rival], one man, [character], is already being named the scholar of the age. You had heard [character] possesses a particular fascination with medicine and anatomy, but when finally you meet, he speaks most of the soul rather than the body. "Imagine a man floating in the air - in such a way that he feels no sensation of pressure or moving air, and sees or hears nothing at all. Such a man could hardly confirm the existence of his physical body, there being no sensations to suggest it. But his soul? That he could hardly doubt. What else is thinking the very question?"

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Surplus

options.text: We will cross that bridge when we come to it.
To prepare for hard times, we must enforce migration to new and fertile lands.

events.text: The recent surplus of Food has encouraged ever more migration into [rival] cities. The question looms, what will happen to this population in the next lean harvest?

events.author: Gabe Campbell
events.name: Tutorial: Tech Deck

options.text: I will choose my Technologies carefully!

events.text: Upon completing the research for a new Technology, you will unlock the next Technology on the Tree (entering it into the discard pile), and four new cards will be drawn from the draw pile of available Technologies for you to select from. After making your new selection from the four drawn cards, the remaining three cards will be sent to the discard pile, and ultimately recycled back into the draw pile when it is empty. Free Unit and Bonus cards are never recycled and are instead permanently discarded if not chosen.

events.author: Gabe Campbell
events.name: Tutorial: Urban Yields

options.text: I will pay close attention to what my Cities produce!

events.text: Cities produce the following Yields: Growth, Training, Civics, Money, Science, Culture, and Happiness. Growth, Training, and Civics are all used for City production. Growth for Civilian Units, Training for Military Units, and Civics for Project and Specialist. When not being used for City production, Training and Civics go to the Global stockpile and Growth goes into the production of new Citizen. Culture and Happiness both go into their respective progress bars. When the Culture bar fills, a positive Event occurs and new Improvement and Wonder are unlocked. When the Happiness bar fills, Growth goes up and Maintenance goes down. Money from cities is added to the Global stockpile, while Science is applied directly as progress toward the nation's research choices.
